docs.title: IoTwin
docs.text: IoTwin is a modular open-source platform for digital twin simulation, visualization, and IoT system integration. Its goal is to bridge physical embedded systems and virtual simulations within a unified environment suitable for research, testing, and real-world development.

docs.title: 💡 Overview
docs.text:
IoTwin consists of two main components:

  1. IoTwin Core (Bus + Simulators)
  2. Written in C11 with a small platform layer (Linux with PREEMPT_RT as real-time target, Windows best effort)
  3. iotwin-bus is a virtual CAN bus over TCP, can_sim a simulated ECU

  4. Built using CMake, tested with Catch2

  5. IoTwin Visualizer (Unreal Engine Project)

  6. Provides real-time visualization of simulated devices and environments
  7. Supports interactive scenarios and rule-based simulations
  8. Useful for training, validation, and system analysis

docs.title: 🧭 Goals
docs.text:
• Provide a flexible development and testing environment for embedded and IoT systems
  • Enable digital twin modeling for realistic device behavior
  • Ensure extensibility, allowing new modules, devices, and visualizations to be added easily

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text:
• Just run the demo: see the Quickstart.
  • Develop: follow the Build Instructions, then read the Architecture Overview and the Bus Protocol.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Status: November 2026 - v0.1.0 released, steps 0-3 implemented and verified on a NUCLEO-G0B1RE

This roadmap merges the two earlier plans - the MVP plan of October 2025 and the post-MVP plan of March 2026 (virtual CAN bus → serial bridge → STM32 CAN controller) - with what the MVP actually delivered.

The project doubles as an embedded learning project, so the ordering puts the embedded topics (MCU, serial, CAN hardware, real-time Linux) before further digital-twin features.

docs.title: Where we are
docs.text: Item Origin Status Virtual CAN bus (TCP software bus, iotwin-bus, can_sim) Mar 2026, phase 1 ✅ done in v0.1.0 Communication layer (gRPC idea) Oct 2025 replaced by the TCP text protocol (ADR 0002) Unreal integration, status display Oct 2025 ✅ as module code (bus subsystem, lamp, switch); not yet a standalone plugin Electrical / load simulation Oct 2025 ⚠️ on/off only, no load, current or fuse ADR: repository structure (mono vs multi repo) Oct 2025 ✅ ADR 0004 Git tag for the MVP Oct 2025 ✅ v0.1.0 Serial bridge PC ↔ MCU Mar 2026, phase 2 ✅ serial_bridge + SLCAN firmware (Firmware) STM32 as CAN controller Mar 2026, phase 3 ✅ FDCAN driver, internal loopback; ⚠️ real bus needs a transceiver + second node SocketCAN bridge step 4 ✅ socketcan_bridge (CAN Tools); live test needs vcan0 Real-time measurements on PREEMPT_RT step 4 ❌ needs PREEMPT_RT hardware DBC, ISO-TP, UDS step 5 ✅ DBC reader + can_monitor, ISO-TP, UDS server in ECU and gateway, uds_client (Diagnostics) Scenarios, more devices, extensions Oct 2025 outlook scenarios ✅ (Scenarios and Faults), more devices open

docs.title: Next phase (agreed November 2026)
docs.text:
The long-term goal is a digital twin that is built from engineering data: circuit diagrams and network descriptions (incl. wireless links) describe the physical setup, the visualizer shows it as a 2D schematic with live bus messages and status, and can switch from there into the 3D scene.

Order of work:

# Feature Notes A Component database ✅ (structure + NUCLEO-G0B1RE) parts and their characteristics for simulation, first entry: NUCLEO-G0B1RE; plus a system description (instances, connections, buses) B Bus / schematic view in Unreal ✅ (first version) 2D view of nodes, buses and live messages, switch to 3D (Visualizer); open: generated from circuit diagrams, wireless traffic, jump to the matching 3D object C UDS diagnostics ✅ on top of ISO-TP: server in ECU and gateway, uds_client, injectable faults as DTCs (Diagnostics); open: SecurityAccess, RoutineControl, flashing D Scenarios and faults ✅ record/replay (candump format), scripted scenarios as tests, bus faults (loss, delay, silence), test bench faults in the ECU (Scenarios and Faults); faults shown in the schematic view; open: per-node bus-off and error frames E More devices and electrical model ✅ (dimmer, current, fuse) dimmable lamp with PWM (also on the NUCLEO LED), electrical model of the output with supply, fuse and smart switch, LAMP_STATUS (Power and Dimming); open: sensors, fan/motor F Real bus and real time transceiver + second node, PREEMPT_RT measurements (needs hardware)

Housekeeping: clearer repository structure, release 0.2.0, Git LFS, branch cleanup (all done). Release 0.3.0 contains features A-E.

docs.title: Order of the post-MVP steps
docs.text: # Step Size Why here 0 Close the MVP ✅ S clean starting point 1 Phase 2a – MCU basics and serial protocol ✅ M no CAN hardware needed yet, core embedded skills 2 Phase 2b – serial_bridge on the PC ✅ S–M connects the MCU to the virtual bus 3 Phase 3 – STM32 as CAN controller ✅ (loopback) L real hardware nodes in the digital twin 4 Real-time Linux and SocketCAN (SocketCAN ✅, RT measurement open) M can run in parallel to 3 5 Protocols on CAN ✅ (DBC, ISO-TP, UDS) M–L builds on 3 and 4 6 Deeper digital twin ongoing lower priority for the learning goal

docs.title: 0. Close the MVP
docs.text:
• Get CI green and merge the MVP pull request, tag v0.1.0.
  • ADR 0004 – repository structure: firmware stays in this repository under firmware/ with its own arm-none-eabi-gcc build (CMake toolchain file), separate from the host CMake build.
  • Optional: move .uasset / .umap to Git LFS before more content is added.

docs.title: 1. Phase 2a – MCU basics and serial protocol
docs.text:
• Nucleo board bring-up: CMake toolchain file, flashing and debugging (ST-LINK / OpenOCD / GDB).
  • UART with interrupt or DMA reception into a ring buffer.
  • Line protocol on the serial link: SLCAN (Lawicel), e.g. t1232DEAD\r. It is the de-facto standard for serial CAN adapters (python-can, SavvyCAN, CANable), so the STM32 later becomes a regular USB-CAN adapter.
  • The SLCAN parser/encoder is portable C shared by host and firmware and unit tested on the host with Catch2.

Done when: frames typed on the PC are echoed by the MCU and decoded correctly on both sides; parser tests run in CI.

docs.title: 2. Phase 2b – serial_bridge on the PC
docs.text:
• New executable that translates SLCAN on a serial port ↔ bus text lines on iotwin-bus.
  • Serial port layer: termios on Linux, Win32 COM ports best effort (ADR 0003).
  • Tested without hardware via socat pseudo-terminal pairs (also in CI on Linux).

Done when: a frame sent from the MCU appears on the virtual bus and vice versa.

docs.title: 3. Phase 3 – STM32 as CAN controller
docs.text:
• bxCAN / FDCAN initialisation, bit-timing calculation (prescaler, time segments, sample point), acceptance filters, RX FIFO interrupt.
  • Error handling: error counters, error-passive, bus-off and recovery.
  • First in loopback mode, then on a real bus with a transceiver (e.g. SN65HVD230) and a second node - a single node on a bus never gets an ACK. The second node can be another board or a USB-CAN adapter.
  • The STM32 acts as gateway: real CAN bus ↔ UART/USB ↔ serial_bridge ↔ iotwin-bus.

Done when: a physical button on the CAN bus switches the lamp in the visualizer, and the ECU's LAMP_CMD drives an LED on the board.

docs.title: 4. Real-time Linux and SocketCAN
docs.text:
• Run the core on a PREEMPT_RT kernel (e.g. Raspberry Pi), compare wake-up latency with a standard kernel (can_sim --stats, cyclictest), document the results in Real-Time Operation.
  • Bridge iotwin-bus ↔ SocketCAN (vcan0 / can0) so can-utils and USB-CAN adapters work directly on Linux.

docs.title: 5. Protocols on CAN (optional)
docs.text:
• DBC files: signals by name instead of hard-coded ids/bits (core and visualizer).
  • ISO-TP (ISO 15765-2) segmentation and flow control, simple UDS services on top - or CANopen, depending on the target domain.

docs.title: 6. Deeper digital twin
docs.text:
• Electrical model with load, current and fuses (ADR on electrical modelling).
  • More devices and sensors, scripted scenarios including fault injection (frame loss, delay, bus-off).
  • Extract the bus integration into an Unreal plugin ("DeviceConnector").

docs.title: Open decisions
docs.text:
• Hardware for steps 1-4: which STM32 board, CAN transceiver, USB-CAN adapter, Raspberry Pi.
  • Working mode for the embedded phases: implemented by hand as a learning exercise with AI review, or AI-assisted implementation.
  • Serial protocol: SLCAN (recommended) or the bus text format.

docs.title: ADR 0001: Choice of Documentation System
docs.text:
Date: 2025-10-07 Context: The project requires long-term maintainable documentation combining developer guides, architecture decisions, and auto-generated API references.

Decision: Use MkDocs + Material for the general documentation and Doxygen for API docs. ADRs will be written in Markdown under docs/adr/.

Consequences: - Single source of truth (Markdown in Git) - Fully static deployable site - Version-controlled documentation with minimal tooling overhead

docs.title: ADR 0002: Virtual CAN Bus Server and Text Line Protocol
docs.text:
Date: 2026-11-13 Status: Accepted (replaces the earlier gRPC idea)

Context: Simulated ECUs (C) and the Unreal Engine visualizer must exchange CAN frames. The first prototype had a simulator acting as TCP client without any server. We need to decide who owns the bus and how frames are encoded on TCP.

Decision:

  1. A dedicated C program, iotwin-bus, is the TCP server and acts as the bus. Every frame a client sends is validated, normalised and forwarded to all other clients - the broadcast semantics of a physical CAN bus. Simulators and the visualizer are equal clients ("nodes").
  2. Frames are encoded as text lines in the compact cansend/candump format (123#DEADBEEF\n), see protocol.

Alternatives considered:

  • Visualizer as server: fewer processes, but every test would need Unreal and only one simulator could connect.
  • Binary frames (16 byte, SocketCAN layout): more compact, but harder to debug and to parse in Unreal; bandwidth is irrelevant at CAN data rates.
  • gRPC: heavy dependency for a stream of 25-byte messages, no benefit for a broadcast bus.

Consequences:

  • The bus can be tested headless in CI (integration tests open real sockets).
  • Any number of simulators, the visualizer and tools like netcat can join.
  • Traffic is human readable; a later bridge to Linux SocketCAN/vcan can reuse the can-utils syntax.
  • The bus adds one TCP hop of latency. Hard real-time timing between ECUs belongs inside the core (see ADR 0003), not on the TCP link to Unreal.

docs.title: ADR 0003: Linux (PREEMPT_RT) as Target Platform, Windows Best Effort
docs.text:
Date: 2026-11-13 Status: Accepted

Context: The core simulation should be able to show realistic real-time behaviour (cycle times, jitter) on a PREEMPT_RT Linux kernel. At the same time the Unreal visualizer is developed on Windows, and running the whole demo on one Windows machine makes development and testing much easier.

Decision:

  • Linux is the reference platform of the C core. Real-time features are implemented for Linux only: SCHED_FIFO priorities, CPU pinning, mlockall() and drift-free cycles with clock_nanosleep(TIMER_ABSTIME).
  • The same sources build on Windows with MSYS2 GCC through a thin platform layer (libs/platform, libs/net/net.*). On Windows the programs run best effort: correct behaviour, but no timing guarantees.
  • Simulation logic (e.g. light_ecu.c) is free of platform code and time sources so it stays portable and unit-testable.
  • Every cyclic loop measures its wake-up latency (--stats N) so the difference between Windows, standard Linux and PREEMPT_RT is visible.

Consequences:

  • Both platforms are built and tested in CI.
  • If real-time requirements grow (e.g. bit-timing accurate arbitration), Windows can be reduced to a demo mode without touching the simulation logic; nothing in the logic may depend on Windows.
  • The TCP link to Unreal is never hard real-time; the visualizer mirrors the state of the bus.

docs.title: ADR 0004: Firmware in the Mono-Repo, Bare-Metal on CMSIS, SLCAN on the Serial Link
docs.text:
Date: 2026-11-13 Status: Accepted

Context: Phases 2 and 3 of the roadmap bring a microcontroller (NUCLEO-G0B1RE, STM32G0B1RE with FDCAN) into the system: it joins the virtual bus over a serial link and acts as a real CAN controller. We need to decide where the firmware lives, how it is built, which abstraction level it uses and which protocol runs on the serial link.

Decision:

  1. Mono-repo: the firmware lives in firmware/ as a separate CMake project with its own toolchain file (arm-none-eabi-gcc). The host build is not affected; CI builds both.
  2. Bare-metal on CMSIS: only the CMSIS core and device headers from ARM and ST are vendored (firmware/vendor). Startup code, linker script, clock, UART and FDCAN drivers are written against the registers - no HAL, no RTOS.
  3. Portable core code is shared and host tested: can_frame, slcan and can_bit_timing (in libs/can) and the application logic (firmware/app/gateway.c, hardware access only through function pointers) compile for the PC and the MCU and are unit tested on the host.
  4. SLCAN (Lawicel) on the serial link, with two documented extensions: l (open in internal loopback mode) and Q (statistics).

Alternatives considered:

  • Separate firmware repository: cleaner boundaries, but shared code (frame model, codec) would need versioning across repositories.
  • STM32 HAL / CubeMX: faster start, but large generated code and less insight into the peripheral; the FDCAN register interface is small enough.
  • Own binary or candump-text protocol on the serial link: SLCAN is the de-facto standard of serial CAN adapters (python-can, SavvyCAN, CANable), so the board is also usable as a generic USB-CAN adapter.

Consequences:

  • The firmware is small (~6.5 KB flash) and every register access is visible.
  • Hardware independent logic is tested without the board; the hardware path is tested end to end on Linux with a pseudo terminal and the real serial_bridge.
  • Supporting another MCU means a new board/ directory plus drivers; the application and the shared code stay unchanged.

docs.title: ADR 0005: Repository Layout - One Repository, Flat Top-Level Areas
docs.text:
Date: 2026-11-13 Status: Accepted

Context: The repository grew from a C simulator to bus server, bridges, tools, firmware, an Unreal project and engineering data. Code lived three levels deep (src/core/can, src/communication/tcp, src/ue/IoTwin, ...) and the layout no longer showed what is a library, what is a program and what is data. The question was whether to split it into several repositories.

Decision: Keep one repository with flat, role-based top-level directories:

Directory Content libs/ shared C libraries: can, log, net, serial, platform apps/ programs: bus (iotwin-bus), can_sim, serial_bridge, socketcan_bridge, can_monitor firmware/ NUCLEO-G0B1RE gateway (own CMake project and toolchain) visualizer/ Unreal Engine project data/ engineering data: DBC files, component database, system descriptions tests/, tools/, docs/ tests, scripts, documentation (incl. docs/Doxyfile)

Why not several repositories:

  • libs/can is compiled into the firmware, the bridges, the tools and the tests; protocol changes touch all of them and must land in one change.
  • One CI run proves that host programs, firmware and tests fit together.
  • A single maintainer pays the cost of versioning shared code across repositories without getting its benefits.

Candidate for a later split: visualizer/ has its own toolchain (Unreal, MSVC), large binary assets (Git LFS) and its own release rhythm. Once the bus protocol is stable it can move into its own repository; it only depends on the documented TCP protocol and the files in data/.

Consequences:

  • Paths are shorter and the role of each directory is obvious.
  • The Unreal project moved from src/ue/IoTwin to visualizer/; local build folders (Binaries, Intermediate, Saved) are not tracked and are recreated on the first build.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
┌──────────────┐   TCP, text lines    ┌──────────────┐   TCP    ┌────────────────────┐
 │   can_sim    │ ───────────────────▶ │  iotwin-bus  │ ◀──────▶ │ IoTwin Visualizer  │
 │ (light ECU)  │ ◀─────────────────── │ virtual CAN  │          │ (Unreal Engine 5)  │
 └──────────────┘                      └──────┬───────┘          └────────────────────┘
                                              │ TCP
                                      ┌───────┴────────┐  USB / SLCAN  ┌────────────────┐  FDCAN
                                      │ serial_bridge  │ ◀───────────▶ │ NUCLEO-G0B1RE  │ ◀──────▶ real CAN bus
                                      └────────────────┘               │ (gateway, B1,  │
                                                                       │  LD4)          │
                                                                       └────────────────┘
        further simulators, tools (netcat, tests) can join as additional nodes
  • iotwin-bus (C): owns the bus. Validates, normalises and broadcasts frames to every other node (ADR 0002).
  • can_sim (C): a simulated ECU with a cyclic control loop. It reacts to the wall switch and commands the lamp relay.
  • Visualizer (Unreal Engine 5.6): a digital twin of the electrical installation. It mirrors bus signals into the scene (relay → power → lamp) and sends user interactions (wall switch) back to the bus.
  • serial_bridge (C) and the NUCLEO-G0B1RE firmware: bring a real microcontroller and its CAN controller onto the virtual bus (Firmware, ADR 0004).

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text:
One repository with flat, role-based directories (ADR 0005):

Path Content libs/can CanFrame + text codec, CanBus FIFO, SLCAN, bit timing, signals/DBC, ISO-TP (partly compiled into the firmware) libs/net portable sockets (net), line framing (line_reader) libs/serial portable serial port (Win32 / termios) libs/platform time, cycle timer, real-time setup, CLI helpers libs/log thread-safe logger apps/bus iotwin-bus server apps/can_sim light ECU and can_sim apps/serial_bridge SLCAN adapter ↔ bus apps/socketcan_bridge Linux SocketCAN ↔ bus apps/can_monitor live bus view with DBC decoding firmware NUCLEO-G0B1RE gateway firmware (separate CMake project) visualizer Unreal Engine project data DBC files, component database, system descriptions tests Catch2 unit, socket and end-to-end tests tools run, flash and packaging scripts docs this documentation, ADRs, Doxyfile

docs.title: can_sim threads
docs.text:
Thread Priority Work main optionally SCHED_FIFO (--rt-*) every tick: read socket (non-blocking), ECU step, send, sleep until the next absolute deadline console normal reads stdin commands, hands frames to the main loop via a CanBus FIFO

The main loop never blocks on the network while connected. Reconnecting (blocking connect) only happens while the bus is unreachable.

docs.title: Visualizer
docs.text: See Visualizer for the Unreal side: the bus subsystem, CAN signal components and the electrical model.

docs.title: Build Instructions
docs.text:
IoTwin has two parts that are built separately:

  1. Core (C, CMake): iotwin-bus, can_sim and the tests.
  2. Visualizer (Unreal Engine 5.6 project in visualizer).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Tool Version Notes GCC 11+ the build enforces GCC; on Windows MSYS2 UCRT64 GCC CMake 3.22+ Ninja used by the CMake presets Git Catch2 is fetched during configure (tests)

Linux (Debian/Ubuntu):

sudo apt-get install -y build-essential cmake ninja-build git

Windows: install MSYS2, then in the UCRT64 shell:

pacman -S --needed mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-cmake mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-ninja git

Make sure C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin is on PATH if you build from PowerShell or Git Bash. The Windows executables are linked statically and run without MSYS2 installed.

Git Bash

Git Bash puts Git's own mingw64/bin in front of PATH. Its older runtime DLLs break the compiler of a recent MSYS2 GCC (it fails silently, CMake reports "compiler is broken"). Prepend MSYS2 in that shell: export PATH="/c/msys64/ucrt64/bin:$PATH".

docs.title: Build and test
docs.text:
cmake --preset gcc-debug          # or gcc-release
cmake --build --preset gcc-debug
ctest --preset gcc-debug

Binaries are placed in build/<preset>/bin/:

Binary Purpose iotwin-bus virtual CAN bus server can_sim simulated light ECU serial_bridge connects an SLCAN adapter (NUCLEO-G0B1RE) to the bus iotwin_tests Catch2 test runner (used by ctest)

Add -DIOTWIN_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=ON to the configure step to treat warnings as errors (CI does this).

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
build/gcc-debug/bin/iotwin-bus
build/gcc-debug/bin/can_sim        # second terminal, type 'help'

All options: --help. Real-time options are described in Real-Time Operation.

docs.title: Firmware (NUCLEO-G0B1RE)
docs.text:
Separate CMake project with an arm-none-eabi-gcc toolchain:

cd firmware
cmake --preset nucleo-g0b1re
cmake --build --preset nucleo-g0b1re

Flashing, wiring and the serial protocol are described in Firmware.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Unreal Engine 5.6 (Epic Games Launcher or source build)
  • Windows: Visual Studio 2022 with the "Game development with C++" workload

docs.title: Open in the editor
docs.text: Open visualizer/IoTwin.uproject. On first open Unreal asks to rebuild the IoTwin module - confirm with Yes. Start the core first, then press Play: the demo scene connects to 127.0.0.1:8080.

docs.title: Build from the command line
docs.text:
& "<UE>\Engine\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat" IoTwinEditor Win64 Development `
    -Project="$PWD\visualizer\IoTwin.uproject" -WaitMutex

Packaging a standalone build is described in Packaging.

docs.title: DBC and can_monitor
docs.text:
data/dbc/iotwin.dbc describes the signals of the light demo:

Id Message Signal Values 0x100 LAMP_CMD (LightECU) LampOn bit 0 0 Off, 1 On 0x200 SWITCH_STATE (WallSwitch) SwitchOn bit 0 0 Off, 1 On

can_monitor shows the bus traffic decoded with a DBC file:

can_monitor --dbc data/dbc/iotwin.dbc --changes

17:51:00.270  100#01                     LAMP_CMD LampOn=1 (On)
17:51:03.689  200#01                     SWITCH_STATE SwitchOn=1 (On)
17:51:03.689  7FF#1234                   (unknown id)

--changes hides cyclic repetitions with unchanged payload.

docs.title: Library (libs/can)
docs.text:
• can_signal.h – signal codec, portable and heap-free (usable in firmware): Intel (little endian) and Motorola (big endian, DBC sawtooth numbering) layouts, signed values, factor/offset, range checks when encoding.
  • dbc.h – reader for BO_, SG_ (incl. multiplexer M / mN), VAL_; extended ids via bit 31; skips everything else, also multi-line comments. Errors are reported with line numbers. dbc_describe_frame() and dbc_set_signal() decode and build frames by name.

docs.title: ISO-TP (ISO 15765-2)
docs.text:
libs/can/isotp.h transports messages of up to 4095 bytes over classic CAN frames (normal addressing), e.g. for UDS diagnostics:

Frame PCI Content Single 0L up to 7 data bytes First 1L LL 12-bit length, 6 data bytes Consecutive 2N sequence number 1..15, 0, ...; 7 data bytes Flow control 3S BS ST CTS / WAIT / OVFLW, block size, STmin

Implemented: flow control with block size and STmin (ms and 100..900 µs encodings), WAIT with WFTmax limit, overflow reporting, N_Bs and N_Cr timeouts, sequence checks, padding (default 0xCC), retry when the CAN driver queue is full. The link is driven by isotp_on_frame() and isotp_poll(now), so it runs on the host and on a microcontroller alike.

IsoTpConfig config;
isotp_default_config(&config, 0x7E0 /* tx */, 0x7E8 /* rx */);
config.send = my_can_send;
isotp_init(&link, &config, rx_buffer, sizeof(rx_buffer));

isotp_send(&link, request, length, now_us);
/* for every received frame: */ isotp_on_frame(&link, &frame, now_us);
/* periodically:             */ isotp_poll(&link, now_us);
if (isotp_receive(&link, &length)) { /* rx_buffer holds a complete message */ }

Tests (tests/test_isotp.cpp) run two links against each other on a simulated bus with simulated time.

docs.title: Recording and replay
docs.text: can_monitor --log FILE records every frame in the candump -L format, can_replay FILE plays it back with the original timing (--speed, --loop, --filter). Logs of a real bus recorded with can-utils work too. Details and scripted scenarios with fault injection: Scenarios and Faults.

docs.title: UDS diagnostics
docs.text:
The UDS server (libs/can/uds.c) and the tester uds_client build on this ISO-TP layer; services, identifiers and trouble codes of the light ECU and the gateway are described in Diagnostics (UDS).

uds_client scan
uds_client --target gateway read 0200

docs.title: SocketCAN bridge (Linux)
docs.text:
socketcan_bridge connects a Linux CAN interface to iotwin-bus. With it the standard can-utils, USB-CAN adapters or a real CAN bus join the virtual bus:

sudo modprobe vcan
sudo ip link add dev vcan0 type vcan
sudo ip link set up vcan0

iotwin-bus &
socketcan_bridge --interface vcan0 &
can_sim &
candump vcan0              # shows 100#00 / 100#01 from the light ECU
cansend vcan0 200#01       # switches the lamp

The live test in tests/test_socketcan.cpp runs when vcan0 exists and is skipped otherwise; CI tries to create it.

docs.title: Component Database
docs.text:
data/ holds the engineering data the simulation and the visualizer build on.

data/
  components/<category>/<vendor>-<part>.json   parts and their characteristics
  systems/<setup>.json                         a concrete setup: nodes, buses, links, messages
  dbc/                                         CAN message definitions
  schema/                                      JSON schemas (editor completion and validation)

Every file references its schema ("$schema"), so editors such as VS Code offer completion and flag mistakes while typing. tools/validate_data.py checks everything including cross references and runs as CTest data_validation in CI.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
One JSON file per part. Example: data/components/boards/st-nucleo-g0b1re.json.

Field Meaning id unique <vendor>.<part>, e.g. st.stm32g0b1ret6 category microcontroller, board, transceiver, sensor, actuator, lamp, relay, switch, power-supply, ... sources datasheets and manuals; every value refers to one of them properties non-numeric facts (core, package, debugger, ...) parameters numeric characteristics (see below) interfaces e.g. fdcan × 2 with tested bitrates ports pins, LEDs, buttons, connectors; connects_to maps board ports to MCU pins contains sub-components (the MCU on a board) simulation hints for the simulators and the visualizer

A parameter has a value or a range, a unit, a source and a verified flag:

"supply_voltage": { "min": 1.7, "max": 3.6, "unit": "V", "source": "st-product-page", "verified": true },
"run_current_64mhz": { "typ": null, "unit": "A", "source": "ds13560", "verified": false,
                       "note": "to fill from the table 'Current consumption in Run mode'" }

verified: false marks values that still have to be confirmed or filled in - the database never pretends to know more than its sources say. Units: V, A, W, Hz, B, bit/s, °C, s, Ω, F, H, lm, %, 1.

docs.title: Current entries
docs.text: Component Status st.stm32g0b1ret6 clock, memory, supply ranges, FDCAN (incl. 500 kbit/s measured in IoTwin), used pins; open: run/stop currents, USART count st.nucleo-g0b1re supply inputs, ST-LINK interfaces (VCP, mass storage), LD4/B1/FDCAN pins; open: measured board current, CN10 pin numbers

docs.title: Systems
docs.text:
A system file describes one setup - which nodes take part, which buses and point-to-point links connect them and which DBC messages they exchange. data/systems/light-demo.json is the demo: light ECU, visualizer and the NUCLEO-G0B1RE gateway on the 500 kbit/s demo bus, the board connected to the PC by USB.

This is the input for the planned 2D schematic view in the visualizer: nodes become boxes, buses and links become lines, messages from the DBC are shown live on them. Later, circuit diagrams and wireless networks are described the same way.

docs.title: Adding a component
docs.text:
1. Copy an existing file into data/components/<category>/.
  2. Fill in sources first, then the values with their source ids.
  3. Run python tools/validate_data.py.

docs.title: Diagnostics (UDS)
docs.text:
The simulated light ECU (can_sim) and the NUCLEO-G0B1RE gateway firmware are diagnosable over the bus with UDS (ISO 14229-1) on top of ISO-TP (ISO 15765-2), like a real vehicle ECU. uds_client is the tester.

uds_client ── iotwin-bus ──┬── can_sim            0x7E0 -> 0x7E8
                           └── serial_bridge ── NUCLEO gateway   0x7E1 -> 0x7E9
functional requests (all ECUs): 0x7DF

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
iotwin-bus
can_sim
uds_client scan                       # identification of the light ECU
uds_client dtc                        # trouble codes (failed or confirmed)
uds_client session extended + write 0103 012C + read 0103   # blink every 300 ms
uds_client --target gateway read 0200 0201 0202             # NUCLEO live data
uds_client                            # interactive, keeps the session alive

uds_client --log-level debug ... shows every CAN frame. In the visualizer's schematic view (TAB) the tester is a node of its own and every diagnostic frame is decoded (DIAG_ECU_REQ SF ReadDataByIdentifier F190).

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
The server (libs/can/uds.c) is portable C without heap use, the same code runs in can_sim and on the STM32.

SID Service Supported 10 DiagnosticSessionControl 01 default, 03 extended (P2 50 ms, P2* 5 s) 11 ECUReset 01 hard, 03 soft 14 ClearDiagnosticInformation FFFFFF (all) or a single DTC 19 ReadDTCInformation 01 count by status mask, 02 by status mask, 0A all 22 ReadDataByIdentifier up to 8 identifiers per request 2E WriteDataByIdentifier extended session only 3E TesterPresent 00
  • suppressPosRspMsgIndicationBit (sub-function | 0x80) for 10, 11 and 3E.
  • Functional requests (0x7DF) are single frames; NRCs 11, 12, 31, 7E and 7F are not sent for them, as the standard requires.
  • S3 timeout 5 s: without requests the server returns to the default session. The interactive tester sends 3E 80 every 2 s.
  • Negative responses: 7F <SID> <NRC>, e.g. 7F 2E 7F (write in the default session), 7F 22 31 (unknown identifier).

docs.title: Light ECU (can_sim, 0x7E0 -> 0x7E8)
docs.text: DID Content Format Access F186 active diagnostic session 1 byte read F187 spare part number ASCII read F189 software version ASCII read F18C serial number ASCII read F190 VIN ASCII, 17 read 0100 lamp output (after protection) 1 byte read 0101 switch input (last SWITCH_STATE) 1 byte read 0102 LAMP_CMD cycle time uint16 ms, 0 = off read / write (0 or 50..60000) 0103 blink period uint16 ms, 0 = off read / write (0 or 50..60000) 0104 supply voltage (measured) uint16 mV read 0105 brightness 1 byte % read / write (0..100) 0106 lamp current uint16 mA read 0107 fuse: blown, heat in % of melting 2 bytes read

docs.title: Faults and trouble codes
docs.text:
Faults are injected on the can_sim console; monitors turn them into DTCs the way a real ECU does:

Console Effect DTC Detected fault short on output switched off (short circuit protection) B1001-11 always fault open on none visible (lamp would stay dark) B1001-13 only while the lamp is on fault supply on DID 0104 drops to 9800 mV B1002-16 always fault overload on 3x current; the 3 A fuse blows after about 2 s B1001-19, B1003-13 while the lamp is on

The faults act on an electrical model of the output (see Power and Dimming); the monitors only see measured current and voltage. fuse replace puts in a new fuse.

dtc on the console shows the ECU's own view. A removed fault leaves the DTC confirmed until it is cleared (uds_client clear). An ECUReset keeps the DTC memory and starts a new operation cycle, like a real ECU.

Status byte (ISO 14229-1 annex D): bit 0 testFailed, 1 testFailedThisOperationCycle, 2 pending, 3 confirmed, 4 testNotCompletedSinceLastClear, 5 testFailedSinceLastClear, 6 testNotCompletedThisOperationCycle. A failed test gives 2F, a cleared DTC 50.

docs.title: Gateway (NUCLEO-G0B1RE firmware, 0x7E1 -> 0x7E9)
docs.text:
Requests reach the gateway from the PC (iotwin-bus -> serial_bridge -> SLCAN) or from a tester on a real CAN bus; responses go to both sides.

DID Content F187 spare part number NUCLEO-G0B1RE-GW F189 firmware version F18C 96-bit unique device id of the STM32 (12 bytes) 0100 last LAMP_CMD (LED) 0101 wall switch (button B1) 0200 TEC, REC, state (0 active, 1 warning, 2 passive, 3 bus off) 0201 uint32 frames to CAN, from CAN, loopback echoes 0202 uint32 uptime in ms 0203 channel open, mode (0 normal, 1 loopback, 2 listen), uint32 bitrate 0204 LED brightness: commanded %, measured % (pin sampling)

DTC U0073-88 (communication bus off) is monitored while the channel is open and not in listen mode.

ECUReset hard restarts the MCU 50 ms after the response (so it can leave UART and CAN); soft resets the counters and keeps the channel to the host open. After a hard reset or a press of the reset button the board's SLCAN channel is closed; serial_bridge notices the rejected frames and configures the adapter again within about a second.

Verified on the hardware: identification incl. unique id, live data, DTC status, soft and hard reset with automatic recovery of the bridge, functional TesterPresent answered by both nodes.

docs.title: Addresses and DBC
docs.text: The diagnostic ids are part of data/dbc/iotwin.dbc (DIAG_ECU_REQ, DIAG_ECU_RESP, DIAG_GW_REQ, DIAG_GW_RESP, DIAG_FUNCTIONAL_REQ, no signals). In data/systems/light-demo.json these messages carry "protocol": "uds", which tells tools such as the visualizer to decode ISO-TP and UDS instead of signals.

docs.title: Not implemented (yet)
docs.text: SecurityAccess (27), RoutineControl (31), communication control (28), download (34/36/37), DTC snapshots and extended data, response pending (78) on the server side. ISO-TP with CAN FD and extended addressing.

docs.title: Firmware: NUCLEO-G0B1RE CAN Gateway
docs.text:
The board joins the virtual bus as a real node and turns the STM32's FDCAN controller into an SLCAN adapter:

 iotwin-bus <-TCP-> serial_bridge <-USB (ST-LINK VCP, SLCAN)-> NUCLEO-G0B1RE <-FDCAN-> CAN bus
                                                                   |
                                                    B1 = wall switch, LD4 = lamp
  • Every frame from the virtual bus is transmitted by the FDCAN controller, every frame received by the controller is reported to the virtual bus.
  • The board is also a node of its own: the blue user button B1 toggles a wall switch (SWITCH_STATE, id 0x200), the green LED LD4 shows the lamp command (LAMP_CMD, id 0x100).
  • Without a transceiver the controller runs in internal loopback mode: frames go through the real CAN peripheral (bit timing, message RAM, interrupts) and are received by the controller itself. These echoes are recognised and not reported a second time.

Design decisions: ADR 0004.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
Function Pin Notes System clock - HSI16 → PLL (M=1, N=8, R=2) = 64 MHz, PCLK 64 MHz Virtual COM port PA2 (TX) / PA3 (RX), USART2 AF1 115200 8N1 via the ST-LINK USB connection FDCAN1 PA12 (TX) / PA11 (RX), AF3 morpho connector CN10; kernel clock = PCLK User LED LD4 PA5 active high User button B1 PC13 active low

LED behaviour: blinking (1 Hz) = firmware running, channel closed (waiting for the bridge); steady = channel open, LED follows the lamp command.

docs.title: Real CAN bus (normal mode)
docs.text: Connect a 3.3 V CAN transceiver (e.g. SN65HVD230) to PA12 (TXD) and PA11 (RXD), terminate the bus with 120 Ω at both ends and add at least one other node - a CAN frame is only acknowledged by another node. Start the bridge with --mode normal. Check the pin positions on CN10 in the board user manual (UM2324).

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
Requires arm-none-eabi-gcc (+ newlib), CMake and Ninja. On Windows with MSYS2:

pacman -S mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-arm-none-eabi-gcc mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-arm-none-eabi-newlib mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-openocd

cd firmware
cmake --preset nucleo-g0b1re
cmake --build --preset nucleo-g0b1re

Output in firmware/build/nucleo-g0b1re/: iotwin_gateway.elf (debugging), .bin / .hex (flashing), .map. Memory use is printed after linking.

docs.title: Flash
docs.text:
./tools/flash-firmware.ps1              # OpenOCD via ST-LINK, falls back to the drive
./tools/flash-firmware.ps1 -MassStorage # copy the .bin to the NOD_G0B1RE drive

Copying iotwin_gateway.bin to the NOD_G0B1RE USB drive works without any debugger driver. Manually with OpenOCD:

openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -f target/stm32g0x.cfg -c "program firmware/build/nucleo-g0b1re/iotwin_gateway.elf verify reset exit"

Debugging: openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -f target/stm32g0x.cfg and in a second terminal gdb-multiarch firmware/build/nucleo-g0b1re/iotwin_gateway.elf → target extended-remote :3333.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Find the COM port ("STMicroelectronics STLink Virtual COM Port" in the Device Manager, /dev/ttyACM0 on Linux), then:

iotwin-bus
can_sim
serial_bridge --serial COM5 --mode loopback --stats 10

or ./tools/run-dev.ps1 -SerialPort COM5. Press B1: the bridge forwards 200#01, can_sim answers with 100#01, LD4 turns on and the lamp in the visualizer lights up.

docs.title: Serial protocol (SLCAN)
docs.text:
Commands end with CR; the board answers CR (ok) or BEL (error). Frames use the same syntax in both directions.

Command Meaning Answer tIIIL<data> send standard frame, e.g. t1002AA55 z TIIIIIIIIL<data> send extended frame Z rIIIL / RIIIIIIIIL send remote frame z / Z S0 … S8 bitrate 10k, 20k, 50k, 100k, 125k, 250k, 500k (default), 800k, 1M CR O open, normal mode CR L open, listen only (bus monitoring) CR l open, internal loopback (IoTwin extension) CR C close CR V / N version / serial number V0100 / NG0B1 F status flags (bit 0 RX queue full, 1 TX queue full, 2 error warning, 3 overrun, 5 error passive, 7 bus error) Fxx Q statistics (IoTwin extension): TX frames, RX frames, loopback echoes (8 hex each), TEC, REC, flags (2 hex each) Q… Z0 / Z1 timestamps - accepted, not implemented CR

Any terminal works for experiments (115200 8N1, send CR): V, S6, l, t100101 → LD4 on.

docs.title: LED dimming (PWM)
docs.text: LD4 (PA5) runs on TIM2 channel 1 (AF2) at 1 kHz. The LED shows the lamp: off, or on with the brightness of LAMP_CMD byte 1 (100 % if the frame has only one byte). board_led_measure_percent() samples the pin for about 5 ms as a self test; UDS DID 0204 reports commanded and measured brightness (see Power and Dimming).

docs.title: Diagnostics (UDS)
docs.text:
The firmware is a UDS server on 0x7E1 -> 0x7E9 (and functional 0x7DF): identification incl. the STM32 unique id, CAN error counters and frame counters, uptime, DTC U0073-88 for bus off, soft and hard ECUReset. The same server code (libs/can/uds.c, isotp.c) is unit tested on the host. Details: Diagnostics (UDS).

uds_client --target gateway scan
uds_client --target gateway read 0200 0201 0202

serial_bridge configures the adapter again when it rejects frames after a reset of the board (UDS hard reset, reset button, power).

docs.title: Code structure
docs.text:
Path Content firmware/board/nucleo_g0b1re/ startup code with vector table (C), linker script, clock/GPIO/SysTick firmware/drivers/uart.c USART2 with interrupt driven RX/TX ring buffers firmware/drivers/fdcan.c FDCAN1: message RAM, bit timing, Tx FIFO, Rx FIFO 0 interrupt, bus-off recovery firmware/app/gateway.c hardware independent application (SLCAN, echo suppression, local node) firmware/app/main.c wiring, button debounce, main loop with WFI libs/can/ can_frame, slcan, can_bit_timing - shared with the host firmware/vendor/ CMSIS core 5.9.0 (ARM) and STM32G0 device headers (ST), Apache-2.0

Bit timing is calculated at run time from the kernel clock: 500 kbit/s at 64 MHz → prescaler 8, 16 tq (1 + 13 + 2), sample point 87.5 %, SJW 2.

docs.title: Tests without hardware
docs.text:
• tests/test_gateway.cpp: application logic against fake hardware.
  • tests/test_slcan.cpp, tests/test_can_bit_timing.cpp: shared code.
  • tests/test_serial_bridge_e2e.cpp (Linux): starts the real serial_bridge, connects it to a pseudo terminal on which the gateway logic runs with a simulated loopback controller, and checks the whole path bus ↔ bridge ↔ board.

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
tools/package.ps1 produces a self-contained Windows release:

dist/IoTwin-<version>-win64/
  bin/                      static MinGW builds, no runtime DLLs needed:
                            iotwin-bus, can_sim, serial_bridge, can_monitor,
                            uds_client, can_replay, can_scenario
  firmware/                 NUCLEO-G0B1RE gateway (.bin, .hex)
  data/                     DBC, component database, systems, scenarios
  Visualizer/IoTwin.exe     cooked Unreal build (Win64)
  start-demo.bat            starts bus, ECU and visualizer
  start-demo-hardware.bat   the same plus the NUCLEO gateway (COM port)
  README.txt, LICENSE
dist/IoTwin-<version>-win64.zip

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• MSYS2 UCRT64 GCC, CMake and Ninja on PATH
  • Unreal Engine 5.6 and Visual Studio 2022 (C++ game workload)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
./tools/package.ps1 -EngineDir "C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.6\Engine"
Parameter Default Meaning -EngineDir $env:UE_ENGINE_DIR Engine folder of the UE installation -Version 0.3.0 used in the package name -Configuration Development Shipping removes logs and the console -SkipVisualizer reuse dist/ue-staging from a previous run -SkipTests do not run ctest -IncludeDebugInfo keep the visualizer .pdb (~350 MB more)

The first cook compiles shaders and takes several minutes; later runs are incremental.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: GitHub Actions builds and tests the core on Linux and Windows for every push and pull request and uploads the binaries as artifacts. The visualizer is not built in CI: GitHub-hosted runners have no Unreal Engine installation, so releases are packaged locally with the script above.

docs.title: Repository size
docs.text: .uasset/.umap files are stored with Git LFS (see .gitattributes). Install Git LFS before cloning (git lfs install), otherwise the Unreal project only contains pointer files.

docs.title: Power and Dimming
docs.text:
The light ECU (can_sim) has a dimmable lamp output with an electrical model, so current, voltage, a fuse and electrical faults behave like on a real control unit. The NUCLEO gateway dims its LED with PWM accordingly.

supply 12.6 V, Ri 50 mOhm -- fuse 3 A slow -- smart high-side switch (PWM) -- 20 mOhm -- 21 W bulb -- GND

docs.title: Dimming
docs.text:
Source How Visualizer mouse wheel: DIMMER_CMD in 10 % steps Any node, scenario send 201#32 (DIMMER_CMD, data[0] = 0..100 %) can_sim console / test bench dim 50 UDS uds_client session extended + write 0105 32

The ECU sends the brightness in LAMP_CMD byte 1 (LampLevel). The visualizer's lamp and the gateway's LED (TIM2 PWM, 1 kHz) follow it. Senders that only send byte 0 still work: receivers treat a missing byte as 100 %.

docs.title: Electrical model (libs/power)
docs.text:
PowerPath is a quasi-static model that is advanced every control step:

  • Supply: open-circuit voltage and internal resistance; the terminal voltage drops with the current.
  • Fuse (3 A, slow blow): I²t model. While the RMS current is above the rating, the excess (I² - In²) * t heats it up. It blows at 40 A²s and cools down at 5 A²s/s below the rating.
  • Smart high-side switch: PWM, current sense, shutdown above 15 A and a retry every 100 ms (thermal restart). Switching the output off resets it.
  • Load: resistive, R = U² / P (21 W at 12 V gives 6.86 Ω, about 1.82 A at 12.6 V).

With PWM the average current is duty * I_on, and the fuse sees the RMS value sqrt(duty) * I_on.

docs.title: Faults and what the ECU sees
docs.text:
Faults change the circuit. The ECU's monitors only use measured values (current sense, supply voltage), like real software:

Fault (fault ... on) Circuit Reaction DTC short load resistance 0 switch shuts down, retries every 100 ms B1001-11 open no load no current although on B1001-13 overload bulb with 3x power (63 W, 5.3 A) overcurrent after 200 ms; fuse blows after about 2 s, lamp dark B1001-19, then B1003-13 supply 9.8 V source supply below 10.5 V B1002-16

A blown fuse stays blown until fuse replace (console or bench ecu fuse replace). Removing the overload alone does not bring the lamp back.

docs.title: LAMP_STATUS (0x101)
docs.text:
Sent by the ECU every 200 ms, Intel byte order (see data/dbc/iotwin.dbc):

Bytes Signal Unit 0-1 LampCurrent mA (factor 0.001 A) 2-3 SupplyVoltage mV (factor 0.001 V) 4 OutputDuty % 5 bit 0 FuseBlown 5 bit 1 Overcurrent (DTC test failed) 5 bit 2 ShortShutdown

The visualizer HUD shows current and voltage from it, the schematic view decodes it at the ECU node.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
DID Content 0104 measured supply voltage, mV 0105 brightness 0..100 % (read/write, extended session) 0106 lamp current, mA 0107 fuse: blown (0/1), heat in % of the melting integral 0204 (gateway) LED brightness: commanded %, measured %

The gateway measures its own PWM: it samples the LED pin's input register for about 5 ms. This checks the real pin and not just the timer registers. Verified on the NUCLEO: 100/50/25/10/0 % commanded gave the same values measured.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text: data/scenarios/light-demo/dimmer.scn and overload-fuse.scn check brightness, current, overcurrent and fuse automatically (CTest scenarios).

docs.title: Bus Protocol
docs.text: All nodes connect to iotwin-bus via TCP (default 127.0.0.1:8080) and exchange CAN frames as text, one frame per line terminated by \n (\r\n is accepted). The server forwards every valid frame to all other connected nodes and drops invalid lines.

docs.title: Frame syntax
docs.text:
The syntax is the compact format of the Linux can-utils (cansend, candump):

Example Meaning 123#DEADBEEF Standard frame, 11-bit id (3 hex digits, max 7FF), 4 bytes 1F334455#11 Extended frame, 29-bit id (8 hex digits, max 1FFFFFFF) 123# Data frame without payload (DLC 0) 123#R Remote transmission request, 123#R4 with DLC 4 123#DE.AD.BE Optional . between bytes (input only)
  • Hex digits are case-insensitive on input; the bus always sends upper case without separators (1ab#de.ad arrives as 1AB#DEAD).
  • At most 8 data bytes (classic CAN). CAN FD (##) is not supported.
  • Lines longer than 255 characters are discarded.

docs.title: Control lines and test bench
docs.text:
Lines that start with ! or @ are not CAN traffic:

Line Meaning !name ecu name of the node in the bus log !testbench on the node wants to receive test bench lines !status counters and active faults: !status nodes=3 routed=120 dropped=4 ... !fault drop P [ID[/MASK]], !fault delay MS [JITTER], !fault silence MS, !fault seed N, !fault clear fault injection of the medium, see Scenarios @<node> <command> test bench command, forwarded only to nodes with !testbench on

The bus answers ! commands only to their sender (!ok, !error <reason>, !status ...). Nodes that never send ! lines never see any of this, so existing nodes (visualizer, serial_bridge) are not affected.

docs.title: Signals of the light demo
docs.text:
Id Name Sender Payload 100 LAMP_CMD can_sim (light ECU) data[0] bit 0: 1 = lamp on; data[1]: brightness 0..100 % 101 LAMP_STATUS can_sim (light ECU) current, supply voltage, duty, flags (Power) 200 SWITCH_STATE Visualizer wall switch data[0] bit 0: 1 = switch on 201 DIMMER_CMD Visualizer (mouse wheel) data[0]: brightness 0..100 %

The ECU sends LAMP_CMD on every change and cyclically (default every 500 ms), so a node that connects later learns the state within one cycle.

docs.title: Serial side
docs.text: Microcontroller nodes are attached through serial_bridge, which speaks SLCAN (Lawicel) on the serial link and translates every frame 1:1 into the bus format above, e.g. t1002AA55 ↔ 100#AA55. The commands are listed in Firmware.

docs.title: Trying it by hand
docs.text:
iotwin-bus --log-frames
can_sim
# in a third terminal (any TCP client works):
nc 127.0.0.1 8080
200#01        <- type this: switch on, the ECU answers with 100#01

On Windows without nc, use ncat (Nmap) or PowerShell, or simply type send 200#01 into a second can_sim console.

docs.title: Real-Time Operation (PREEMPT_RT)
docs.text: Linux is the target platform for timing-accurate simulation (ADR 0003). Windows builds behave identically but without timing guarantees.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Both iotwin-bus and can_sim accept:

Option Effect (Linux) --rt-priority N SCHED_FIFO with priority 1..99 for the main loop --rt-cpu N pin the main loop to CPU core N --rt-lock-memory mlockall(MCL_CURRENT \| MCL_FUTURE) - no page faults later

can_sim additionally has --tick-ms N (loop period, default 10 ms) and --stats N (log wake-up latency every N seconds).

On start both programs log whether the kernel is PREEMPT_RT (/sys/kernel/realtime) and which settings could be applied.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Real-time scheduling and memory locking need privileges. Either run with sudo, or grant them once:

sudo setcap cap_sys_nice,cap_ipc_lock+ep build/gcc-release/bin/can_sim

or via /etc/security/limits.conf:

@realtime  -  rtprio   90
@realtime  -  memlock  unlimited

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
iotwin-bus --rt-priority 70 --rt-lock-memory &
can_sim --tick-ms 1 --rt-priority 80 --rt-cpu 2 --rt-lock-memory --stats 5

Typical output line:

loop 1 ms: 5000 cycles, wake-up latency min/avg/max = 0.004/0.011/0.038 ms, overruns: 0

The maximum latency is the relevant figure. On a standard kernel under load it can reach milliseconds; on PREEMPT_RT it typically stays in the tens of microseconds. WSL2 and Windows are not suitable for such measurements.

docs.title: Scenarios and Faults
docs.text:
IoTwin can disturb the virtual bus on purpose and check how the nodes react, like a hardware-in-the-loop test bench:

  • Fault injection of the medium in iotwin-bus: lost frames, delay and jitter, a silent bus.
  • Test bench commands to simulated nodes, e.g. a short circuit at the lamp output of the light ECU.
  • Recording and replay in the can-utils candump -L format.
  • Scenario scripts (can_scenario) that drive all of this and check the reactions, including UDS diagnostics. They run as automatic tests.
iotwin-bus
can_sim
can_scenario data/scenarios/light-demo/lamp-short-dtc.scn

RUN  Short circuit of the lamp output becomes DTC B1001-11
PASS Short circuit of the lamp output becomes DTC B1001-11 (12 steps, 124 ms)

docs.title: Scenario scripts
docs.text:
One step per line, # starts a comment (200#01 inside a frame is not a comment). Times are in milliseconds.

Step Meaning name <text> name shown in the output (default: file name) send <frame> put a frame on the bus, e.g. send 200#01 expect <pattern> [within <ms>] a matching frame must arrive (default 1000 ms) expect-not <pattern> for <ms> no matching frame may arrive wait <ms> let time pass bench <node> <command> test bench command to a simulated node, e.g. bench ecu fault short on bus <fault> fault of the bus: drop, delay, silence, seed, clear (see below) uds <target> <request> [expect <response>] UDS request to ecu, gateway or TX:RX (hex ids) log <text> print a note

An expect sees the frames since the start of the last action (send, bench, bus, uds), including those that arrived while the action was still running (e.g. a reaction sent before the UDS response), and consumes them up to its match, so two expect in a row need two frames. wait discards what arrives during the wait.

Frame patterns: 100#01 exact payload, 100#01* payload starting with 01, 100#* any payload, 100#XX01 XX = any byte, 100#R remote frame, 8-digit ids for extended frames.

UDS: request and expected response are hex bytes (spaces allowed); a trailing * allows more bytes. Without expect the step needs a positive response. Example: uds ecu 190209 expect 59027F9001112F - exactly the DTC B1001-11 with status 2F. Services and identifiers: Diagnostics.

Exit code 0 when all scenarios passed, 1 if one failed, 2 for a syntax error. A failure names the line and what was seen instead:

  FAIL line 1: expect 100#01 within 600 ms
       not seen within 600 ms (last frames: 100#00)

Single steps without a file: can_scenario -e "bus drop 20" -e "bus delay 30 10". --verbose prints every step and every frame.

docs.title: Bus faults
docs.text:
bus ... Effect drop <percent> [<id>[/<mask>]] lose frames; optionally only matching ids (hex), e.g. drop 100 200 drops every 0x200 delay <ms> [<jitter ms>] deliver late; frames never overtake each other (as on CAN) silence <ms> nothing gets through, e.g. a disturbed or short-circuited bus seed <n> start value of the random generator: the same seed loses the same frames clear remove all faults (frames still delayed keep their place)

Faults affect every node, including the scenario runner. The bus logs who injected what; !status (see Bus Protocol) reports the counters of dropped and delayed frames.

docs.title: Test bench commands
docs.text:
bench <node> <command> sends @<node> <command> over the bus. Only nodes that registered for the test bench receive it, never the CAN nodes. can_sim registers as ecu (--name changes it) and runs the command like one typed on its console:

Command Effect fault short on/off lamp output short to ground: output switched off, DTC B1001-11 fault open on/off open load: DTC B1001-13 while the lamp is on fault supply on/off supply voltage low: DTC B1002-16 fault overload on/off bulb with three times the power: DTC B1001-19, the fuse blows (B1003-13) fuse replace put in a new lamp fuse dim <0..100> brightness fault clear remove all injected faults lamp on/off/toggle, blink <ms>/off operate the ECU directly

docs.title: Recording and replay
docs.text:
can_monitor --log drive.log --quiet      # record everything on the bus
can_replay drive.log                     # play it back with the original timing
can_replay --speed 4 --loop --filter 100 drive.log

The log format is the one of candump -L, so logs from a real bus (can-utils on Linux, candump -L can0 > drive.log) can be replayed onto iotwin-bus and IoTwin logs can be played on a real bus with canplayer:

(1794606835.444395) iotwin 200#01
(1794606835.445622) iotwin 100#01

docs.title: Scenarios of the light demo
docs.text:
data/scenarios/light-demo/ (automatic test scenarios in CTest):

Scenario Checks switch-controls-lamp SWITCH_STATE -> LAMP_CMD within 300 ms cyclic-lamp-cmd 500 ms cycle; cycle 0 via UDS = only on change diagnostics-identification VIN, sessions, write protection, blink via UDS, reset lamp-short-dtc injected short: output off, DTC failed and confirmed, cleared frame-loss lost SWITCH_STATE: the lamp does not react bus-delay 250 ms delay adds up in both directions bus-silence silent bus: nothing arrives, the ECU continues afterwards dimmer DIMMER_CMD -> brightness in LAMP_CMD, duty and current in LAMP_STATUS overload-fuse overload: overcurrent DTC, fuse blows, replaced fuse brings the lamp back

tools/run_scenarios.py starts a fresh iotwin-bus (free port) and can_sim for every scenario, so faults, DTCs and settings never leak into the next one:

python tools/run_scenarios.py --bin build/gcc-debug/bin data/scenarios/light-demo

data/scenarios/hardware/gateway-diagnostics.scn checks the NUCLEO gateway and needs the board with serial_bridge; it is not part of the automatic tests.

docs.title: Protocol details
docs.text: The control and test bench lines extend the bus protocol without affecting existing nodes: a node only receives them after it has sent a ! command itself or registered with !testbench on. See Bus Protocol.

docs.title: Visualizer (Unreal Engine)
docs.text: The Unreal project lives in visualizer (UE 5.6, C++ module IoTwin).

docs.title: Bus integration (Source/IoTwin/Bus)
docs.text:
Class Role FCanFrame CAN frame struct + text codec (same format as the C core) FIoTwinBusConnection worker thread: TCP connection, auto-reconnect, line framing UIoTwinBusSubsystem game-instance subsystem: SendFrame, OnFrameReceived, OnConnectionChanged, last value per id UCanSignalComponent maps one bit of a frame to a bool (Receive or Transmit)

Connection settings (Config/DefaultGame.ini):

[/Script/IoTwin.IoTwinBusSubsystem]
Host=127.0.0.1
Port=8080
bEnabled=True

Command line overrides: -IoTwinBusHost=<host>, -IoTwinBusPort=<port>, -IoTwinBusDisabled.

docs.title: Binding a signal in Blueprint
docs.text:
Add a Can Signal component to any actor, set Direction, Can Id (hex, e.g. 100), Byte Index and Bit Index.

  • Receive: bind to On Value Changed or read Get Value.
  • Transmit: call Set Value; the frame is sent on change, after a reconnect, and optionally every Transmit Cycle Seconds.

For full frames use the subsystem directly (Get IoTwin Bus Subsystem → Send Frame / On Frame Received).

docs.title: Schematic view (Source/IoTwin/Schematic)
docs.text:
TAB (or the button in the HUD) switches between the 3D scene and a 2D schematic of the system:

  • nodes from the system description (data/systems/*.json), the CAN bus with its members, other links (USB) as dashed lines;
  • every frame is decoded with the DBC of the bus and shown at the node that sent it, with a dot travelling over the bus to the consumers;
  • status per node (green < 3 s, yellow < 10 s since its last frame), frame rate, message log;
  • click a node for details: description, messages it sends/receives, links and the characteristics from the component database (unverified values are marked);
  • diagnostic frames ("protocol": "uds" in the system description) are decoded as ISO-TP/UDS, e.g. DIAG_ECU_REQ SF ReadDataByIdentifier F190;
  • faults injected into the bus (see Scenarios) turn the bus red with the active faults and the number of lost and delayed frames. The visualizer asks iotwin-bus with !status once per second and registers as visualizer (NodeName in [/Script/IoTwin.IoTwinBusSubsystem]).
Class Role FSystemDescription loads a system JSON (nodes, buses, links, messages) FCanDatabase DBC reader for the visualizer (messages, signals, value tables, Intel/Motorola) FComponentCatalog reads data/components/**/*.json, formats values (1.7 .. 3.6 V, 64 MHz) UIoTwinSchematicSubsystem model: loads the data, follows OnFrameReceived / OnFrameSent, attributes frames to nodes, view switch FSchematicRenderer draws the view on the HUD canvas (layout designed for 900 px, scaled)

Which node sent a frame: frames sent by this game belong to SelfNode (visualizer); for received frames the first producer of the message in the system description other than SelfNode is used (iotwin-bus does not echo frames back to their sender).

[/Script/IoTwin.IoTwinSchematicSubsystem]
SystemFile=data/systems/light-demo.json
SelfNode=visualizer

SystemFile is searched relative to the launch directory, the repository root (visualizer/..) and the package root. Command line: -IoTwinSystem=<file>, -IoTwinView=Schematic (start in the schematic), -IoTwinSelectNode=<node id> (preselect a node, e.g. for screenshots).

docs.title: Dimming and power
docs.text: The mouse wheel dims the lamp: the visualizer sends DIMMER_CMD (0x201) in 10 % steps, starting from the brightness in the last LAMP_CMD. The power source reads that brightness from LAMP_CMD byte 1 (LevelByteIndex), its port carries it as SupplyLevel, and the lamp's light intensity and bulb colour follow UElectricalDeviceComponent::PowerLevel. The HUD shows the brightness and the ECU's measured current and supply voltage from LAMP_STATUS (0x101), plus fuse, overcurrent or short circuit.

docs.title: Electrical model (Source/IoTwin/Systems)
docs.text:
• UElectricalPortComponent: wiring is a symmetric list of ports stored on both ends (saved with the level). HasPower() searches the wiring graph for a supplying port; cycles are handled.
  • APowerSourceActor: supply with an output relay. With Controlled By Can the relay follows its RelayControl signal (default 0x100 byte 0 bit 0).
  • AElectricalCableActor: two conducting ends, drawn with CableComponent; ConnectBetween(A, B) positions and wires it.
  • ALampActor: port → UElectricalDeviceComponent → ULightEmitterComponent and a bulb that changes colour.
  • AWallSwitchActor: clickable switch that transmits its position (0x200).

Older assets that only stored ConnectedPort are migrated automatically when the component is registered.

docs.title: Demo scene
docs.text: AGM_Simulation (the default game mode) builds the light demo at runtime from engine basic shapes, so it works in any map and needs no extra assets. To build your own scene, create a Blueprint subclass of GM_Simulation, untick Spawn Demo Scene (the relay and switch ids are configurable there as well) and select it as GameMode Override in the map's World Settings.

docs.title: Tests and smoke runs
docs.text:
# Automation tests (CAN codec, DBC, system description, component database)
UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe visualizer/IoTwin.uproject -ExecCmds="Automation RunTests IoTwin;Quit" -unattended -nullrhi

# Unattended game run: screenshot after 10 s, quit after 15 s
UnrealEditor.exe visualizer/IoTwin.uproject -game -IoTwinScreenshot=10 -IoTwinQuitAfter=15

# Same in the schematic view with the gateway selected
UnrealEditor.exe visualizer/IoTwin.uproject -game -IoTwinView=Schematic -IoTwinSelectNode=gateway -IoTwinScreenshot=10 -IoTwinQuitAfter=15

The screenshot is written to Saved/Screenshots/IoTwinDemo.png.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
The light demo shows the whole chain: a simulated control unit (ECU) switches a lamp via a CAN bus, and an Unreal Engine visualizer mirrors the installation as a digital twin.

wall switch (Visualizer) --200#01--> iotwin-bus --> can_sim (light ECU)
lamp relay  (Visualizer) <--100#01-- iotwin-bus <-- can_sim (light ECU)

docs.title: Windows release package
docs.text:
1. Download and unzip IoTwin-<version>-win64.zip.
  2. Double-click start-demo.bat.
  3. In the visualizer click the wall switch (or press SPACE); the mouse wheel dims the lamp (Power and Dimming). Press TAB for the 2D schematic: nodes, CAN bus and USB link with every message decoded at its sender; click a node for its details.
  4. Diagnose the ECU like a workshop tester: uds_client scan, then type fault short on in the CAN-Sim window and run uds_client dtc (see Diagnostics).
  5. Disturb the bus and watch the reaction: can_scenario -e "bus drop 50" loses every second frame, can_scenario -e "bus clear" ends it; ready-made test scripts are in data/scenarios (see Scenarios).

Three windows open:

Window Content IoTwin Bus every frame on the bus IoTwin CAN-Sim the light ECU - type commands here IoTwin 3D view with status panel and recent bus traffic

Commands in the CAN-Sim window:

Command Effect lamp on / lamp off ECU switches the relay blink 500 ECU toggles the lamp every 500 ms (blink off) send 123#DEADBEEF put any frame on the bus status, help, quit

docs.title: With a NUCLEO-G0B1RE
docs.text:
The board becomes a real CAN node of the demo: its blue button B1 is a second wall switch, its green LED LD4 shows the lamp.

  1. Copy firmware\iotwin_gateway.bin to the NOD_G0B1RE USB drive of the board (LD4 starts blinking: firmware runs, waiting for the PC).
  2. Look up the COM port ("STMicroelectronics STLink Virtual COM Port" in the Device Manager).
  3. Run start-demo-hardware.bat COM5 (your port).

Press B1: the lamp in the visualizer and LD4 turn on. Details and wiring for a real CAN bus: Firmware.

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
cmake --preset gcc-debug
cmake --build --preset gcc-debug

Then on Windows:

./tools/run-dev.ps1          # starts iotwin-bus and can_sim

and open visualizer/IoTwin.uproject in Unreal Engine 5.6 and press Play. See the Build Instructions for details.

docs.title: Core on Linux, visualizer on Windows
docs.text:
For real-time experiments the core runs on a (PREEMPT_RT) Linux machine and the visualizer connects over the network:

BIND=0.0.0.0 tools/run-core.sh          # on Linux

Visualizer\IoTwin.exe -IoTwinBusHost=<linux-ip>

See Real-Time Operation.
